page.layout: One column of verse and epigrams, full width. Running head at top left-centre, page number at top right. No margin notes, catchword or signature.

p.i: Gignit: sed caufas doceant qui femina rerum / Quíque arcana tenent interiora viri.
Num maiora vides hominum portenta creari? / Quà cælum multò mitius, atque solum est?
Testis culta novem studiis Europa sororum, / Quæ tota princeps erigit orbe caput.
Hîc quàm horrenda vigent, pudor est memorare, libellis
Ut possit nostris maior adesse fides.

main_text.head: IN QUENDAM COGNO-mine Curionem, vere Dromonem.

p.i: NON venit à cura, quæ nulla est, Curio, nomẽ: / A Curro melius Currio dictus erit.

main_text.head: AD PAULUM.

p.i: Quod tibi non sapiunt aliena poemata, Paule, / Non mirum est, aliis nam tua nil sapiunt.

main_text.head: IN LIBRUM MARTINI Marlorei Causidici Barrensis, cui titulum fecit De Orthodoxo Baptismo & Calviniano.

p.i: QVI leget hæc, verè poterit tum dicere, toto / Marlorenus libro nil nisi causidicus.

page.notes: Printed "Caluiniano" and "Baptismo" normalised (u as consonant v; long s as s). "nomẽ" kept with its tilde as printed. "Marlorenus" read from a small scan; a mark over the e may be present and is not certain. Verse lines are set as one paragraph per couplet, with "libellis" a continuation of the line before it. The "alienapoemata" join is a spacing irregularity in the print, read as "aliena poemata".
